text.title: C# .NET Core Backend Core Rules
text.summary: 19 testable rules grounding the .NET Core service umbrella — HTTP surface, DI, EF Core, background work, tests, configuration and security hygiene. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale.

rule.statement: Every async controller action and service method MUST accept `CancellationToken` as the last parameter and thread it to every downstream IO call (EF, HttpClient, channel reads).

rationale.source: Microsoft async guidelines + internal load-test postmortems

rule.rationale: Without token plumbing, client disconnects and server timeouts do not cancel database queries, causing thread-pool starvation under load.

rule.statement: Register `DbContext` as Scoped, `IHttpClientFactory`-backed clients as Transient, hosted services as Singleton. Resolve scoped dependencies inside a `BackgroundService` via `IServiceScopeFactory.CreateScope()` — never via constructor injection.
rule.rationale: BackgroundService is singleton; injecting a scoped DbContext into its constructor throws at runtime on first use (or worse: silently shares state across iterations).

rule.statement: Forbid `.Result`, `.Wait()`, `GetAwaiter().GetResult()`, and `async void` (except for top-level event handlers). Reviewers MUST reject diffs that introduce any of these.
rule.rationale: Sync-over-async deadlocks under a synchronisation context; `async void` swallows exceptions and crashes the host.

rule.statement: EF Core read paths MUST call `AsNoTracking()`, and MUST add `AsSplitQuery()` when a query carries more than one collection `Include`. Bulk operations MUST use `ExecuteUpdateAsync`/`ExecuteDeleteAsync`. Repositories MUST NOT return `IQueryable<T>` — materialize with `ToListAsync`/`ToArrayAsync` before crossing the layer boundary, and return `PagedResult<T>` (Items + TotalCount + Page + PageSize) from list methods.
rule.rationale: Change tracker bloats memory on read-only paths and read queries are ~30% faster without it; two collection `Include`s in one JOIN multiply rows into a Cartesian explosion. Leaked `IQueryable` lets controllers append arbitrary LINQ that bypasses the intended constraints, or execute against a disposed context. `PagedResult` keeps callers from duplicating the count query.

rule.statement: Error responses MUST conform to RFC 7807 ProblemDetails. Register `AddProblemDetails()` in `Program.cs`; never return ad-hoc anonymous error envelopes from controllers.
rule.rationale: A single error contract lets clients (mobile, BFF, partners) implement one parser; ad-hoc envelopes multiply parsing logic.

rule.statement: Source MUST be organised by feature (`Features/Users/{UsersController.cs, UserService.cs, UserDtos.cs, UserMappings.cs}`), not by technical layer (`Controllers/`, `Services/`, `Dtos/`).
rule.rationale: Feature folders keep cohesive changes in one directory; technical-layer trees scatter a single feature across five folders and hide the surface area from the agent.

rule.statement: Every controller carries `[ApiController]` and `[Route("api/v1/[controller]")]`. Actions that can return a non-200 status return `ActionResult<T>`; `IActionResult` is used only where the response type genuinely varies at runtime. POST actions that create a resource return `CreatedAtAction(...)`.
rule.rationale: `[ApiController]` turns on automatic model-validation binding and ProblemDetails error responses. `ActionResult<T>` lets Swagger infer the success schema without a `ProducesResponseType` per action, and `CreatedAtAction` emits the 201 + Location header clients expect.

rule.statement: Constructor-inject interfaces only, never concrete implementations, and register each service interface as Scoped in `Program.cs`. Cap a controller or service at 4-5 constructor dependencies; beyond that, split the responsibility or move to a mediator/handler. Never inject `IServiceProvider` into a controller or service to call `GetService<T>()` inside a method — the one exception is a `BackgroundService`, which must create scopes manually.

rationale.source: Microsoft DI docs + internal review audit

rule.rationale: Concrete injection blocks test doubles. The service-locator pattern hides dependencies from the constructor signature, so the container cannot validate them at startup and unit tests cannot mock them. Six or more dependencies is a god-class signal the agent will keep feeding.

rule.statement: DTOs are `record` types. Service methods never return an EF Core entity across the service boundary — map to a DTO first.
rule.rationale: Entities carry EF tracking state and navigation proxies. Returning them leaks persistence concerns into the controller and produces infinite recursion in JSON serialization once a navigation property is loaded. Records give value semantics, immutability and `with`-expressions.

rule.statement: Every entity mapping lives in an `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` class applied via `modelBuilder.ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(...)` — not in data annotations on the entity.
rule.rationale: Configuration classes keep persistence concerns out of the domain entity. Annotations couple the domain model to EF-specific attributes and block reuse outside an EF context.

rule.statement: `SaveChangesAsync()` is called only inside the repository or a unit of work — never directly in a service method. The service orchestrates; the repository owns the persistence boundary.
rule.rationale: A service calling SaveChangesAsync bypasses the repository abstraction and makes batching several operations into one unit of work impossible without leaking the EF context up a layer.

rule.statement: In-process background work uses `BackgroundService` + a bounded `Channel<T>` registered as Singleton, with a scope created per work item inside `ExecuteAsync`. Periodic work uses `PeriodicTimer.WaitForNextTickAsync(ct)` — never `Thread.Sleep` and never `Task.Delay` in a loop.
rule.rationale: A Channel gives back-pressure the loop cannot silently drop; a per-item scope keeps the scoped DbContext out of the singleton. `PeriodicTimer` fires on wall-clock interval without drift even after a slow tick, and returns false on cancellation, so shutdown needs no extra coordination.

rule.statement: `Program.cs` ends with `public partial class Program { }` in any service that has integration tests.
rule.rationale: `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` takes `Program` as a generic argument, so the type must be visible to the test assembly. Without the partial declaration the test project fails to compile with "Cannot find type Program".

rule.statement: Unit tests mock the service interface (`Mock<IUserService>`), pass `mock.Object` to the controller, and assert the shape with `Assert.IsType<T>` before casting to the inner value. Integration tests use `IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>` and obtain the client via `factory.CreateClient()` — never a bare `HttpClient` pointed at localhost.
rule.rationale: Mocking the interface isolates the HTTP-layer assertions (status code, ActionResult type, DTO shape) from the database. `IClassFixture` shares one in-process test server across the class, and `CreateClient()` routes through it without a real socket, which is what makes the suite deterministic and fast.

rule.statement: Every project sets `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` and `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>`, and pins the SDK in `global.json` so CI and local builds agree. `CS4014` (un-awaited Task) and the `CS8` nullability warnings are build failures, not noise.

rationale.source: Microsoft .NET docs + internal async review audit

rule.rationale: A forgotten `await` on `ToListAsync()` serializes the Task itself (`{"Result":null,...}`) and is invisible without CS4014 as an error. Nullability warnings left as warnings accumulate until they carry no signal.

rule.statement: Configuration is bound through `IOptions<T>` with `.ValidateDataAnnotations().ValidateOnStart()`. Do not read `IConfiguration["Section:Key"]` ad hoc in business code.
rule.rationale: Binding from appsettings is loose: a typo in a section name yields a default-valued object rather than an exception, so the service starts and misbehaves. ValidateOnStart converts that into a startup failure.

rule.statement: Do not call `Task.Run` inside a controller action, a service method on the request path, or a middleware. Offload real background work to a hosted service.
rule.rationale: `Task.Run` on the request path steals a thread from the same pool that serves requests, so it adds latency instead of removing it, and the work is lost on shutdown.

rule.statement: Connection strings, API keys and tokens never land in `appsettings.json`. Use `dotnet user-secrets` locally and environment variables or a managed secret store in production; a pre-commit grep blocks connection strings.
rule.rationale: `appsettings.json` is committed and distributed to every developer machine and CI environment; a secret placed there is disclosed the moment the repo is cloned, and rotating it means a deploy.

rule.statement: `[AllowAnonymous]` and wildcard CORS policies are never added to unblock a development error. Every new `[AllowAnonymous]`, `[Authorize(Roles = ...)]` and CORS policy is a named human checkpoint in review.
rule.rationale: `[AllowAnonymous]` on a controller disables authorization for it in production builds too, and a `*` CORS origin allows credentialed cross-origin requests. Both survive review unless flagged explicitly, because the diff looks like a one-line config change.

rule.statement: Entity or configuration changes ship with the matching `dotnet ef migrations add`; CI fails when `Migrations/` is out of sync with the model snapshot. A destructive migration is reviewed as SQL via `dotnet ef migrations script` before it runs, and `dotnet ef database update` is never pointed at a shared or production database by an agent.
rule.rationale: Agents edit the entity and forget the migration, so the drift surfaces at deploy. A dropped column that production still reads is an outage, and the only cheap gate is a human reading the generated SQL.
